findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() — unwrap on I/O Result panics on missing file, permission error, or unreadable path
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path causes thread panic instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, Error> and use map_err(|e| Error::Io(e)) or equivalent typed error

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() — unwrap on parse Result panics on non-numeric value
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV row aborts the entire session load instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: use map_err(|_| Error::Invalid) on the parse call and return Result<Vec<Record>, Error>

findings.problem: as u16 lossy cast from u32 parse result — values exceeding u16::MAX (65535) silently truncate
findings.failure_mode: a value of 70000 becomes 34464 with no error, corrupting domain data silently
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parts[1].parse::<u32>()?).map_err(|_| Error::Overflow) or parse directly as u16 via u16::from_str

findings.problem: parts[0] — unchecked indexing into Vec with no bounds check before access
findings.failure_mode: a line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields panics with index out of bounds
findings.fix: use split_once(',') and ok_or(Error::Invalid) to handle missing fields without indexing

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) — logging/I/O side effect inside a data-loading function that should be a pure parser
findings.failure_mode: hidden side effects break determinism, make testing harder, and couple the core to stdout
findings.fix: move logging to the shell layer; load_sessions should return data only with no println or other I/O

findings.problem: parts: Vec<String> collects all split parts into owned Strings unnecessarily — allocates on every line
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocations per line increase memory pressure and GC pressure for a simple two-field parser
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',') with &str slices via split_once, or use get() on split() iterator to avoid intermediate Vec

findings.problem: Record uses String for name — no domain newtype or validation on the name field
findings.failure_mode: empty, whitespace-only, or invalid names can be constructed freely; no type-level enforcement of name invariants
findings.fix: introduce a Name newtype with a fallible constructor that validates non-empty, or at minimum validate at the parse boundary

findings.problem: No benchmark exists for load_sessions throughput or memory usage
findings.failure_mode: cannot verify performance claims or regression for file I/O and CSV parsing path
findings.fix: add a criterion or similarly structured benchmark measuring parse throughput and allocation count

findings.problem: No profiler evidence (flamegraph, perf, or similar) for this module
findings.failure_mode: hot paths like Vec allocation per line and parse calls are unprofiled
findings.fix: run flamegraph or perf record and attach the report showing allocation hotspots

findings.problem: No allocation analysis (e.g., heaptrack, jemalloc profiling) showing per-line Vec<String> allocation pattern
findings.failure_mode: hidden O(n) intermediate allocations where zero-allocation parsing is feasible
findings.fix: run allocator profiling to quantify allocations and verify that split_once + &str fix reduces them to zero intermediate allocs

findings.problem: No test file exists in the crate to verify behavior contract
findings.failure_mode: regressions in parsing, error handling, and overflow behavior go undetected
findings.fix: add integration or unit tests covering valid rows, missing fields, non-numeric values, overflow values, and missing files

missing_evidence: no profiler data for hot paths
no test file to verify behavior contract
residual_risk: static review only — no commands run. Four BLOCKERs (unwrap on I/O, unwrap on parse, lossy cast, unchecked indexing) must be fixed before delivery. Hidden println I/O breaks functional core purity. Zero allocation safety (try_reserve) not applicable at current scale but should be reviewed if input size grows.
